s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dysphagia with weight loss and respiratory symptoms
salient_findings: Progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids
Weight loss of more than 100 lbs
Episodes of food getting stuck in the throat
Hoarseness and tongue paralysis with atrophy
key_facts: 60 pack-year history of tobacco use
Progressive dysphagia over a three-month period
Weight loss of more than 100 lbs
Night sweats
Hoarseness
Tongue paralysis with atrophy on cranial nerve testing
Cachexia and exaggerated cervical lordosis
Productive cough without fever, chest pain, or hemoptysis
Large confluent anterior cervical osteophytes on CT
Bilateral noncalcified pulmonary nodules at lung apices
Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes on CT
Diffuse innumerable pulmonary nodules predominantly in lung bases on CT
Modified barium swallow study showed reduced laryngeal and hyoid excursion
Flexible laryngoscopy showed large retropharyngeal mass partially obstructing airway

shortlist.label: Hypopharyngeal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive dysphagia, weight loss, and hoarseness are common symptoms of hypopharyngeal cancer, and the patient's 60 pack-year history of tobacco use increases the risk

shortlist.label: Oropharyngeal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms to hypopharyngeal cancer, and the patient's tobacco use history also increases the risk for oropharyngeal cancer

shortlist.label: Laryngeal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Hoarseness and tongue paralysis are symptoms that can be associated with laryngeal cancer, and the patient's tobacco use is a significant risk factor

shortlist.label: Esophageal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive dysphagia and weight loss are key symptoms of esophageal cancer, and the patient's age and tobacco use history increase the risk

shortlist.label: Mediastinal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes on CT and systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss can be indicative of mediastinal lymphoma

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive dysphagia, weight loss, night sweats, hoarseness, and tongue paralysis with atrophy are consistent with hypopharyngeal cancer. The large retropharyngeal mass partially obstructing the airway on flexible laryngoscopy and the extrinsic compression of the upper esophagus on EGD also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oropharyngeal cancer
rejected.why: While possible, the symptoms and findings are more consistent with hypopharyngeal involvement

rejected.label: Laryngeal cancer
rejected.why: Mobile vocal cords on flexible laryngoscopy make this less likely

rejected.label: Esophageal cancer
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings suggest a more proximal lesion, such as hypopharyngeal cancer

rejected.label: Mediastinal lymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of a large retropharyngeal mass and the patient's symptoms are more suggestive of a primary head and neck cancer
